“The higher consumers perceive positive e-retailers’ ethics, the more they are loyal to the online stores.”Originality/value – The paper contributes to the e‐retailing literature by examining the impact of cultural context on e‐retailer's ethics, and the influence of ethics on consumers' loyalty intention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ethical issues that arise in e-commerce and how these issues affect consumer attitudes and intentions to shop with an online retailer.
the impact of cultural context and the ethics of online retailing on e‐retail consumers’ attitudes, and how this impacts their intention to shop at an online store again.
the impact of cultural context on e‐retail consumers' perceptions of online retailers' ethics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the findings of this research are consistent with the hypothesis that consumers with horizontal individualism and vertical collectivism are more likely to hold positive perceptions of online retailers’ ethics.

this research study has provided a significant contribution towards the understanding of how the cultural orientation influences the perceptions of the ethics of online retailer (CPEOR) and the e-loyalty of the consumers in the Taiwanese context.
the findings of this study provide empirical evidence that cultural orientation has an impact on consumers' perception of e-retailers' ethics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the relationship between cultural orientation and consumer perception of online retailers’ ethics is moderated by the type of collectivism.
we have developed and tested a model that explains how the cultural context influences the perception of e-retailers’ ethics and how this perception affects e-loyalty intention.
we have developed a model of the antecedents of e-loyalty and tested the model in an Asian setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cultural orientation of e-shoppers influences their perceptions of online retailers’ ethics, and these perceptions in turn influence consumers’ loyalty intention to online shopping.
the cultural orientation of the e-shopper influences his/her perceptions of the ethics of the e-retailer.

consumers with different cultural backgrounds may perceive the same e-retailer differently in terms of ethics, and that e-loyalty intention is positively influenced by the perception of e-retailers' ethics.
